text:
### Observed differences

- The main difference concerns two trios of activities that behave as alternatives. In the earlier window, A16, A17 and A18 each appeared in about 75 in 100 traces, while A19, A20 and A21 each appeared in about 25 in 100; in the later window these shares flipped, with the first trio at about 25 in 100 (49 of 200 traces) and the second at about 75 in 100 (151 of 200). None of the six activities repeats within a trace in either window. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- The trios were mutually exclusive before and remain so later: cross-pairs such as A16–A19 or A17–A20 never occur in the same trace in either window, while members of the same trio occur together whenever that trio runs. Within the A19–A21 trio, both execution orders appear in similar shares in both windows, so the internal ordering is unfixed before and after. [REL009, REL014, REL018, REL007, REL022, REL023, REL025]
- The branch point sits at A15. Earlier, about 75 in 100 of A15's observed outgoing continuations led to A16, A17 or A18 and about 25 in 100 to A19, A20 or A21; in the later window this is reversed (about 76 in 100 to A19–A21, about 24 in 100 to A16–A18). A15 also runs before the selected trio in both windows: A15 before A16–A18 in about 75 in 100 traces earlier, and A15 before A19–A21 in about 76 in 100 later. [DIR001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- A25 tracks whichever trio is selected. Earlier it co-occurred with A16, A17 or A18 in about 75 in 100 traces (usually after them) and with A19–A21 in about 25 in 100; later it co-occurred with A19–A21 in about 76 in 100 (about 40 in 100 strictly after, about 36 in 100 interleaved) and with A16–A18 in about 25 in 100. [REL012, REL017, REL021, REL024, REL026, REL027]
- A minor positional shift: among traces containing both A15 and A19, the gap between them was mostly one event position earlier (about 54 in 100) and became a flatter spread with three positions most common later (about 39 in 100); this concerns event positions, not clock time. [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the choice after A15 between two alternative three-activity paths shifted its shares: in the later window about 75 in 100 traces continue with A19, A20 and A21 (previously about 25 in 100), while A16, A17 and A18 run only in the remaining minority (about 25 in 100, previously about 75), with A25 executing after whichever path is taken. This rests on direct routing and relational evidence: A15's outgoing transitions redistributed exactly in step with the participation flips, the trios remained mutually exclusive, and A15 still preceded and A25 still followed the selected trio — so activities were neither dropped, added, nor bypassed, and only the branch shares moved. Chance is an unlikely explanation as a whole: 35 items qualified against roughly 0.53 expected for 106 tested units if nothing had changed, every item's difference exceeded 199 of 200 random re-splits, and the underlying supports are large (about 150 vs 49 and 50 vs 151 traces out of 200). Two limitations remain: all items describe one underlying rerouting and are therefore not independent confirmations, and the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows sampled a different mix of cases that simply routes differently, rather than a changed routing decision at A15 itself. [OCC001, OCC004, DIR001, REL004, REL009, REL024]

Other differences: the A15–A19 positional-gap shift noted above is consistent with the branch flip changing which traces contain this pair, and does not by itself indicate that an activity was moved. [LAG001]
